## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
In modern scholarship, Andrea Schlosser references the Khuddakanikāya commentary on this poem (*Vakkalittheragāthāvaṇṇanā*), which glosses the verbal form *viharissāmi* as abiding in the bliss of the path (*maggasukha*), fruition (*phalasukha*), and extinction (*nibbānasukha*) by cultivating the factors of awakening (*bodhipakkhiyadhammā*) [Schlosser 2016].
Curated parallels recorded by SuttaCentral include passage-level correspondences with the *Mahāpajāpatigotamītherīgāthā* (Thig 6.6) in the Therīgāthā and verses 21–30 of the Gāndhārī Dharmapada (G3-Dhp) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus detects extensive Pali-internal text reuse between this poem (§1.2–5.5) and both the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* and the *Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā*, as well as a substantial overlap (§0.1–3.2) with the *Nhātakamunittheragāthā* (Thag 6.11) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language automated alignments, DharmaNexus additionally records machine-generated matches with the Sanskrit *Catuṣpariṣatsūtra*, notably between segment §2.4 and its opening text [DharmaNexus].
